summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every Hindi video gets 400-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 30 views. The best videos explain a 'dumb-looking' machine or sensor with a surprising claim (clap switch, gyro robot, PIR sensor, line follower), and they earn more likes and saves. Generic 'how does X work?' videos about doors, taps, smoke detectors and touchscreens get little attention, and the one English video did not reach Instagram at all.
winningPattern: Robot/maker-project subjects (clap switch, gyro balancing robot, PIR, line follower, IR obstacle robot) with a surprising or 'it can't actually do what you think' Hindi hook, titled as a bold statement ('X Nahi, Sirf Y Sunta Hai', 'Gyro Ke Bina Ye Robot Turant Gir Jaata') rather than a plain question. Posted on Instagram Reels first, where reach is 5-20x higher than YouTube. Saves and shares come from concrete builds students can copy, while everyday-appliance explainers underperform.
doMore: Make Arduino/robot build-based videos (balancing, line follower, obstacle avoidance) with a bold 'it has no brain / can't see' claim
Use statement-style Hindi titles with a twist instead of 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔'
End with a save-worthy prompt like 'Save karo, project banana hai' and show the module name and wiring
Prioritize Instagram Reels and post there first; cross-post to YouTube with a stronger first-frame hook
Continue the clap switch, PIR and gyro series as follow-ups (Part 2, build guide)
stopDoing: Generic everyday-appliance explainers (tap, mall door, lift, smoke detector) with the same question-style title
Posting near-duplicate topics (two IR sensor, two smoke, two tap videos) within days of each other
